adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration sets cook_method default to 1 (raw_html) instead of 0 (regular), so existing and new posts are treated as raw_html and normal posts stop being cooked, rendering raw markdown to users

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration adding `posts.cook_method` with `default: 1`. In Discourse, `Enum.new(...)` maps the first symbol to `1` (not `0`), consistent with existing usage like `Post.types ||= Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`. Therefore `default: 1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Only posts explicitly created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (as in `TopicEmbed.import`) will skip cooking. The proposed finding incorrectly assumes `1` means `raw_html` and that normal posts would stop being cooked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsanitized external HTML rendered raw: imported posts cooked with raw_html bypass sanitization and embed view outputs <%= raw post.cooked %>, allowing stored XSS from third-party RSS feed content via PollFeed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a path where third-party HTML is stored and later rendered without sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed` pulls `i.content` from an external RSS/ATOM feed and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` (after only `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `scrub`, neither of which sanitizes HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` explicitly bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`return raw`), which is where Discourse would normally sanitize content. Finally, the embed template renders it as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore an attacker controlling (or injecting into) the feed content can persist arbitrary HTML/JS and have it rendered (stored XSS), at least in the embed view and likely anywhere the post is displayed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: e.data.height is never validated as a number, allowing arbitrary string assignment to iframe.height

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler does set `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` without explicitly coercing/validating `e.data.height` as a number. However, the only sender introduced in this diff (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb) posts `document.body.offsetHeight`, which is a numeric value, so the normal code path is already numeric. Also, assigning an arbitrary string to `iframe.height` (with a hard-appended "px") does not create script injection; it would at worst yield an invalid/odd height value and the origin is checked. As a result, this is more of a hypothetical robustness nit than a clear, verifiable bug/security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js has no null/undefined guards for #discourse-comments, discourseUrl, or discourseEmbedUrl, causing silent embed failure with uncaught errors

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, it unconditionally does:
- `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then `comments.appendChild(iframe);` — if the element is missing, `comments` is `null` and this throws a runtime error.
- It also unconditionally reads `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` when building `iframe.src`. If either global is not defined on the host page, referencing it causes a `ReferenceError` (undeclared variable) and the script stops.
There are no null/undefined guards or fallbacks, so the finding describes a real failure mode present in the diff.

topic_retriever.rb uses non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE; if process dies between them the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed URL — should use SET NX EX

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` method `retrieved_recently?`, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. Because these are two separate Redis commands, if the process (or connection) dies after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without an expiry. After that, `setnx` will always fail for that `embed_url` and the method will return `true` (treating it as retrieved recently) forever, permanently throttling retrieval for that URL. This is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race on concurrent import of same URL: two jobs can both see embed.blank? and create duplicate topic/post; unique index conflict on TopicEmbed.create! aborts transaction with no rescue/retry

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: it first queries `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if `embed.blank?` it creates a topic/post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. With concurrent calls for the same `url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so the loser will raise a uniqueness/record-not-unique exception. There is no rescue/retry handling in `import`, so this can abort the job/request path and surface as an error (even if the transaction rolls back the extra post). This race is directly implied by the diff and the unique constraint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic title is never updated on re-import; changed RSS article titles leave stale titles forever

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `title` argument is only used when creating a new topic/post (`PostCreator.new(... title: title, ...)`). When an existing `TopicEmbed` is found, the update path only revises the post raw (`PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, ...)`) and updates `content_sha1`, but never updates the topic title (or first post title) even if the feed/article title changes on re-import. Since `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `i.title` on every poll, changed titles would remain stale indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed invalid URL fallback substitutes i.id which may be blank or a non-URL tag id (UUID/URN), causing import to silently return nil and items to be dropped without logging

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the URL is set to `i.link` and then replaced with `i.id` when the link is blank or not an http(s) URL (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Many feeds use `id` as a URN/UUID (e.g., `urn:uuid:...`) or may have it blank, which will then be passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. In TopicEmbed.import, the first line is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so such items are silently skipped/dropped with no logging. This is a concrete behavior directly implied by the diff.

If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., job errors, remote fetch fails, feed misconfigured), the client will keep reloading and stay on the loading page indefinitely because there is no terminal failure state or backoff in the view/controller logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed#poll_feed iterates every feed item with no limit, doing per-item DB lookups and full import transactions — no pagination/batching, vulnerable to large feeds

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `rss.items.each` with no cap (no `take(n)`, date cutoff, or paging) and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item. `TopicEmbed.import` performs at least one DB query per item (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and may run a DB transaction + post creation/update per item. This is a verifiable unbounded workload: a large feed can make the scheduled job run excessively long and do many DB operations in one execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever runs the entire feed poll synchronously inside request-triggered jobs, re-parsing the whole remote feed per cache-miss embed request

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items`. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` on embed cache-miss, which runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, so each cache-miss embed request can synchronously fetch and re-parse the entire remote feed within that job. The throttling key is per `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so different embed URLs can still trigger repeated full feed polls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 60-second per-URL throttle allows unbounded job enqueues and outbound fetches for arbitrary distinct URLs, enabling work-queue fill and outbound-request amplification

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` with no throttling or deduplication. The only throttle is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which is a 60-second Redis key scoped to the full `@embed_url` (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`). That means an attacker can (a) enqueue an unbounded number of jobs by varying `embed_url` values (distinct URLs => distinct keys => no throttle), and (b) for valid-host URLs (`invalid_host?` only checks host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), trigger unbounded outbound `open(url)` fetches in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicRetriever#fetch_http`. Even repeated requests for the same URL can still fill the work queue since throttling happens after dequeue, not at enqueue time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX followed by EXPIRE in retrieved_recently? can leave a key with no TTL, permanently wedging retrieval for a URL if the process dies between calls

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code does `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process/thread crashes or is killed after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE executes, the key will exist without a TTL. On subsequent calls, SETNX will fail and the method will return `true`, causing retrieval to be throttled forever for that embed_url. This is a real correctness/availability issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in poll_feed.rb is computed but never used — dead code; conditional GET/modified-since optimization never wired up

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` computes and memoizes a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but there are no references to `feed_key` anywhere in `PollFeed` (or elsewhere in the diff). The polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of this key, so as introduced in this diff it is unused/dead code. The specific claim about conditional GET/If-Modified-Since intent is not directly proven, but the “computed but never used” part is verifiably true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import re-hashes full content with SHA1 and re-parses with Nokogiri (absolutize_urls) on every poll even when unchanged; parse could be deferred until after hash comparison

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the SHA1 is computed for every call, but Nokogiri parsing via `absolutize_urls` is only invoked in two cases: (1) when the embed is new (`embed.blank?`) and (2) when the content hash differs (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`). On unchanged polls for an existing embed, the method computes `content_sha1` and then skips the update block, so it does not re-parse with Nokogiri. Therefore the finding misreads the diff: the parse is already deferred until after the hash comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default of 1 for cook_method makes all posts default to raw_html, breaking Markdown rendering sitewide and creating a stored-XSS surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `Post.cook_methods` as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`. In this codebase, existing enums (e.g. `Post.types = Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`) conventionally map the first symbol (`:regular`) to `1`, not `0`. The new logic in `Post#cook` only returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and the RSS/import path explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` for those imported posts. Therefore the migration default of `1` makes posts default to `:regular` cooking, not `:raw_html`, so it does not break Markdown rendering sitewide as claimed. (There may be separate XSS concerns around raw HTML for imported content, but that is not caused by the default=1 behavior asserted in the finding.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb postMessage targetOrigin breaks when request.referer is nil, becoming postMessage(..., '') so the iframe never resizes

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the request is rejected when `request.referer` is nil/blank because `URI(request.referer || '').host` becomes `nil`, which will not equal `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. Therefore the `embed` layout (and its `postMessage` call) is never rendered in the nil-referer case, so it cannot "becoming postMessage(..., '')" and cause a resize failure as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes calling .scrub on nil when feed items lack content, aborting the whole poll run since retry is false
CGI.unescapeHTML in PollFeed double-decodes entities, corrupting imported content

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before importing. `CGI.unescapeHTML` performs a single entity decode pass; if `i.content` is already decoded/plain HTML, it is effectively a no-op for most inputs. The proposed finding claims “double-decodes entities” and “corrupts imported content,” but nothing in this diff shows a second decoding step or demonstrates that `SimpleRSS.parse` already decodes such that this call would reliably corrupt data. Any assertion about SimpleRSS’s internal decoding behavior would be speculative beyond what’s verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses indexOf prefix/substring match instead of exact origin equality, weakening security
embed.js iframe.src concatenation silently produces a broken route if discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash, and the discourseUrl contract is undocumented

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the iframe URL is built via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with `/` (e.g., `https://forum.example.com`), the resulting URL becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is clearly malformed. The diff does not show any normalization or enforcement of a trailing slash for `discourseUrl`, so the code as introduced is brittle and can break depending on the provided value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController#best raises a 500 on deleted/unreadable topics instead of responding gracefully

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when a topic_id is returned it unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no explicit handling for missing/deleted/inaccessible topics. However, the proposed finding claims this will "raise a 500" for deleted/unreadable topics, and that is not verifiable from this diff: the behavior depends on TopicView and global controller exception handling (e.g., whether RecordNotFound/InvalidAccess is rescued into 404/403). The diff itself does not demonstrate that a 500 will occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor removes the --category/-c option without deprecation, breaking existing scripts/CI invoking -c

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed and all logic that reads `options[:category]` and derives `category_id` is deleted. The import path no longer accepts or uses a category argument, so any existing automation invoking `disqus:import -c <category>` would now fail with an unknown option or silently lose the ability to set category. No deprecation or compatibility handling is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor#revise! switches to save(validate: !skip_validations), silently skipping validations for existing callers passing :skip_validations for other purposes

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning callers that explicitly pass `skip_validations: true` will now actually skip validations. However, the option name strongly implies that intent, and the only new/visible caller added in this diff (TopicEmbed.import) passes `skip_validations: true` specifically for imported content. The claim that existing callers pass `:skip_validations` “for other purposes” is not supported by anything verifiable in the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: posts.cook_method migration default is 1 (raw_html), so all new posts skip markdown cooking and return raw unrendered HTML (post.rb:131, migration default: 1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1`. In Discourse-style `Enum.new` usage, the first symbol maps to `1`, so `default: 1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. The new `Post#cook` only skips cooking when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which would require explicitly setting that value (as done in `TopicEmbed.import`). Therefore the finding misreads the default and is not a real problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw unrendered post HTML in best.html.erb is an XSS vector since posts bypass the markdown/sanitization pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, where `contents` can come directly from RSS (`PollFeed`: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) without any HTML sanitization (only relative URL rewriting). In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, it renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which for these posts will be the unsanitized `raw` HTML. Therefore, if a feed item contains malicious HTML (e.g., `<script>` or event handlers), it can be executed in the embed context: a real XSS vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeout on open-uri HTTP fetches in topic_embed.rb:55 and poll_feed.rb:32, allowing Sidekiq workers to hang indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using `open-uri` without specifying timeout options: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). These calls do not pass `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (or similar), so Sidekiq jobs depend on defaults and can block for long periods if the remote host is slow/unresponsive, tying up workers. The lack of explicit timeouts is directly verifiable in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on feed items lacking 'content' (i.content.scrub), and with retry: false silently aborts processing for that hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each RSS item is processed with `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item does not have a `content` field (common for some RSS feeds that only provide `description`/`summary`), `i.content` will be `nil`, and calling `scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-run (no rescue/guard is present). Additionally, the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a crash will not be retried by Sidekiq, meaning that run's processing stops until the next scheduled execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No per-item error handling in PollFeed loop; any exception stops processing of remaining feed entries

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, rss.items.each do |i| processes each entry without any begin/rescue. If any iteration raises (e.g., i.content is nil causing NoMethodError on `i.content.scrub`, CGI.unescapeHTML issues, or TopicEmbed.import raising), the exception will abort the job and prevent remaining feed items from being processed. There is no per-item error handling to isolate failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading page reloads every 30s forever and never surfaces failure when embed import fails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view contains JS that unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms. There is no timeout limit, backoff, or alternate render path when the background retrieval fails permanently (e.g., network error in `open(url)`, parsing error, invalid/missing `embed_by_username`, etc.), so the page can reload indefinitely without surfacing any failure to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic job has no failure feedback path; TopicRetriever bails silently leaving the embed page stuck on loading, and non-staff failed imports block retry for 60s per URL

adjudication.rationale: Yes, this behavior is present in the diff. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it always enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading`, whose JS reloads the page every 30s with no terminal failure state. In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, retrieval is skipped if `retrieved_recently?` is true; `retrieved_recently?` sets a Redis key (`setnx` + `expire 60`) before `perform_retrieve` runs. So if `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` fails to create a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., exception in `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, or misconfig like missing `embed_by_username` causing `fetch_http` to return), the embed remains missing and the page keeps reloading, while non-staff retries are throttled for up to 60 seconds per URL regardless of whether the previous attempt succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redis throttle setnx/expire is non-atomic; process death between them leaks a key that permanently blocks retrieval for non-staff — should use SET with EX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses two separate Redis commands: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process/thread dies (or raises) after setnx succeeds but before expire runs, the key can be left without a TTL. In that case, subsequent calls will see the key present, skip the setnx branch, and return `true` forever (for non-staff, since staff can bypass via `no_throttle`). This is a real correctness issue caused by the non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE pattern; using a single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` (or equivalent) avoids it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key cache variable in poll_feed.rb is unused dead code; the 'feed modified' check doesn't exist so feeds are re-imported hourly even when unchanged

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is introduced (building a Redis-like cache key using the feed URL) but it is never referenced anywhere in the file or in the shown diff. There is also no logic that uses this key (or any Last-Modified/ETag handling) to skip polling/import when the feed is unchanged; `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates items hourly. While `TopicEmbed.import` will dedupe/update by `embed_url` and `content_sha1`, the job still fetches/parses the feed and attempts imports every hour regardless of modification, so the finding about the missing 'feed modified' check is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: discourse_expires_in 1.minute caching headers apply to the loading render, potentially causing CDN/browser caching of the loading page

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` call is unconditional and occurs after the `render 'loading'` branch. In Rails, execution continues after `render` unless you `return`, so the loading response will also get a 1-minute cache lifetime. That can cause browsers/CDNs to reuse the cached loading page even after the topic has been retrieved, delaying the switch from loading to actual content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses indexOf instead of strict comparison, accepting prefix-matching origins like https://evil-discourse.com
spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:36-44 — tests only verify mocks, not real view rendering; mock tests cannot catch the latent NoMethodError when @topic_view.topic is nil with empty posts

adjudication.rationale: The controller sets `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` only when `topic_id` is present; otherwise it renders `loading`, so `best.html.erb` is not rendered without `@topic_view`. In real execution, `TopicView.new` (a normal constructor) will return an instance, not nil, and the diff provides no evidence that `@topic_view.topic` can be nil. The spec does mock `TopicView.new` without specifying a return value (which would be nil in many mocking libs) and does not `render_views`, so it could hide a view error *in the test setup*, but that is a test smell rather than a verifiable runtime bug introduced by the diff. The claimed “latent NoMethodError” is speculative and not demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:2-6 — empty posts array edge case untested; no test covers real TopicView behavior (hidden/deleted topics, secure categories) for the unauthenticated embed endpoint

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an embed endpoint and view logic that already guards the empty-posts case via `@topic_view.posts.present?` checks in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. The proposed finding is primarily about missing/insufficient test coverage for authorization/TopicView edge cases (hidden/deleted topics, secure categories) rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. The provided controller spec does cover the empty-posts branch indirectly (it stubs `TopicView.new` but doesn’t exercise TopicView internals), but lack of “real TopicView behavior” tests is not itself a concrete bug/security issue demonstrated in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:33-39 — delegation test only; actual poll_feed implementation including the i.link/i.id fallback logic is untested

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` gates and delegates to `poll_feed` (lines 33-39), but there are no tests for `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` itself, which contains the main logic (RSS parsing, `i.link`/`i.id` URL fallback, content handling, and calling `TopicEmbed.import`). That means the fallback logic and core behavior introduced in this diff is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for new job Jobs::RetrieveTopic (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb): InvalidParameters raise, user lookup, and no_throttle staff behavior are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Sidekiq job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` in `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, but the added spec files cover `Jobs::PollFeed`, `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, and `TopicEmbed` only. There is no `spec/jobs/retrieve_topic_spec.rb` (or any spec referencing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), so behaviors like raising `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `embed_url` is missing, the optional user lookup by `user_id`, and passing `no_throttle` based on `user.staff?` are not tested anywhere in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:31-46 — throttle tests mock retrieved_recently? instead of testing real redis setnx/expire logic; perform_retrieve paths (RSS-check, exists?, fetch_http bail-outs) have no coverage

adjudication.rationale: The spec does stub `retrieved_recently?` (and therefore doesn’t exercise the real Redis `setnx/expire` throttling logic), and it also doesn’t cover the various internal branches inside `perform_retrieve` (RSS path, early return when embed exists, fetch_http bail-outs). However, this is about test completeness/coverage rather than a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff; the production code can still be correct even if these paths aren’t explicitly tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor#revise! behavioral change (lib/post_revisor.rb:82-84) introducing skip_validations option with no spec covering skip_validations: true

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, enabling a `skip_validations` option. However, this is not a verifiable defect by itself (it’s an intentional feature to support embedded/RSS imports), and the claim that there is “no spec covering skip_validations: true” is not accurate: `TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` exercises the update path (“Supports updating the post”). While it doesn’t explicitly assert validations are skipped, the code path using `skip_validations: true` is executed in specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook raw_html short-circuit (app/models/post.rb:131-134) has no spec verifying normal posts are unaffected and no security test that raw HTML posts don't escape the sanitizer
ensure_embeddable edge cases untested (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-31): malformed referer rescue path has 0% coverage, plus referer scheme/host edge cases

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_embeddable` with a `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch, and the new controller spec does not explicitly exercise a malformed `request.referer` that would trigger that rescue. However, the proposed finding asserts “0% coverage” and broader scheme/host edge cases, which cannot be verified from the diff alone (no coverage data is shown), and “untested edge cases” is not itself a concrete defect/bug/security issue in the introduced code. The code’s behavior for malformed referers is explicitly handled via the rescue and raising `InvalidAccess`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls edge cases untested: non-standard ports, protocol-relative URLs, and javascript: hrefs passing through unsanitized

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the conversion condition is `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')`. This mistakenly treats protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` as “relative” and rewrites them to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x`, which is incorrect behavior for a common URL form. Also, the import path sets `cook_method: :raw_html` (bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline) and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so hrefs such as `javascript:...` (and other dangerous HTML coming from RSS/remote content) are not sanitized by this method and can pass through unchanged. Tests only cover simple `/path` rewriting, not these cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus thor task behavioral change (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:141-146): --category option removed and import switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote with no test and unannounced CLI interface change

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category` in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The import logic is changed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept or apply a category, so the previous behavior (allowing `--category` to control where topics are created) is lost and the CLI interface is no longer backward-compatible. No tests are added/updated for this Thor task change in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote has no test: open(url).read (SSRF-relevant), readability tag whitelist, and opts[:title] fallback untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which calls `open(url).read` and applies a tag/attribute whitelist, and there are no specs directly exercising `import_remote` (existing specs cover `TopicEmbed.import`, `TopicRetriever`, and `Jobs::PollFeed`). However, the proposed finding is primarily “missing tests” rather than identifying a concrete defect introduced by the diff. Lack of unit tests is not itself a verifiable bug/security flaw in the code, and the diff does include host validation in `TopicRetriever` before calling `import_remote` in the embed flow. So while the statement about coverage is true, it doesn’t point to a definite, demonstrable problem in behavior/security from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131219203905 defaults cook_method to 1 (raw_html) but regular is 0; normal posts may skip cooking entirely since PostCreator never sets cook_method (needs confirmation, 0-indexing not shown in diff)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not verify that `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` is 0-indexed. In fact, existing code already uses `Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` for `Post.types`, and in Discourse this custom Enum is typically 1-based (e.g., regular post type stored as 1). If the Enum is 1-based, `default: 1` correctly maps to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so normal posts will still be cooked. The finding’s core claim (that 1 == raw_html and regular == 0) is therefore a misread/speculation not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default sets cook_method to 1 (raw_html) for all posts, so normal Markdown posts bypass the cooking pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `Post.cook_methods` as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and adds a migration setting `cook_method` default to `1`. In this codebase, `Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` is already used for `post_type`, and Discourse stores `post_type` for regular posts as `1`, implying the first enum value maps to `1` (not `0`). Therefore `cook_method` default `1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so normal Markdown posts do not bypass the cooking pipeline by default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever synchronously invokes Jobs::PollFeed inline in HTTP request path including blocking network fetch

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` does **not** call `TopicRetriever` on the HTTP request path; it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` does synchronously call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, and `PollFeed` performs a blocking network fetch via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, but that happens inside the background job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, not inline during the HTTP request. Therefore the finding’s claim about occurring in the HTTP request path is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated host-validation logic between embed_controller.rb and topic_retriever.rb with slightly different semantics

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two host checks: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` validates the *request referer* host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` validates the *embed_url parameter* host against the same setting. Although this is “duplicated” in the sense that both touch host validation, they intentionally apply to different inputs (referer vs embed_url) and act as defense-in-depth. The semantic differences (controller raises, retriever just treats as invalid and no-ops) are not a verifiable bug/correctness defect in this diff; they don’t contradict each other in a way that breaks behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: PollFeed#feed_key defined and memoized but never used

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` is defined and memoized (`@feed_key ||=`) but nothing in the diff calls `feed_key`. `execute` calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` performs parsing/importing without referencing `feed_key`. There are no other references to `feed_key` elsewhere in the provided diff, so it is unused (dead code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed assumes every feed item has :content; raises NoMethodError for items with only description/summary, and retry: false kills the whole run

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each RSS item is processed with `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item does not have a `content` field (common for many RSS feeds that only provide `description`/`summary`), `i.content` will be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise a `NoMethodError`, aborting the job. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so such a failure will not be retried by Sidekiq, making the import brittle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: XSS/origin weakness in embed.js: indexOf substring match allows origins containing discourseUrl as substring; arbitrary height applied
embed.js assumes #discourse-comments element exists with no null check, throwing on misconfigured pages

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the script does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be null and `appendChild` will throw a runtime error. There is no guard/early return in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb interpolates raw request.referer into inline JS string; unescaped quotes/newlines break the script
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root problem: raw `request.referer` is inserted into an inline JavaScript string without proper escaping. The candidate focuses on broken JS due to quotes/newlines, but that is the same unescaped interpolation issue that enables XSS when attacker-controlled content is injected into the JS context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing newline at EOF on multiple new files

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly shows “\ No newline at end of file” on several files (e.g., app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb, lib/topic_retriever.rb, and an edited migration). So the observation is factually verifiable. However, a missing trailing newline is a formatting/style issue and not a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the change in typical Ruby/Rails execution, so it doesn’t qualify as a “REAL problem” under the given criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to unrelated migration 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts without explanation

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` only changes whitespace (removes trailing spaces) and adds a missing newline at EOF; it does not add `force: true`. The only `force: true` addition in the diff is in `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`. Therefore the proposed finding is based on an incorrect reading of the diff and is not a verifiable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method migration default of 1 maps to raw_html enum value, causing all existing and new posts to skip markdown rendering pipeline

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. In Discourse, these `Enum.new(...)` enums are conventionally 1-based (the first symbol maps to 1, second to 2), matching how existing enums like `Post.types` work. The migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`, which therefore corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Only posts explicitly created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (as done in `TopicEmbed.import`) will skip the cooking pipeline. So the finding misreads the enum/default mapping and is not a verifiable problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics changed with force: true, silently dropping and recreating table and destroying all aggregated topic statistics with no backup

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it again. adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import mutates caller's string via contents << and computes SHA1 after appending 'imported from' footer, so content_sha1 never matches source content and locale string changes trigger spurious rewrites

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the method appends the “Imported from” footer using `contents << ...`, which mutates the caller’s string in place, and then computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` after that append. As a result, `content_sha1` is a hash of the locally-modified content (including the I18n translation and formatting of the footer), not purely the source article content. This means changes to the footer (e.g., locale/translation string changes) can change the SHA1 and trigger the “content changed” path (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`) even if the remote content is unchanged. The claim that it “never matches source content” is overstated, but the core issue (hash includes appended footer + mutation) is real and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attacker-controlled SSRF: /embed/best?embed_url with spoofed Referer header causes server to fetch arbitrary internal HTTP URLs and publish contents as public topic

adjudication.rationale: The controller gate (`ensure_embeddable`) relies on `request.referer`, which can be spoofed by a non-browser client, but the actual network fetch is performed later by `TopicRetriever#import_remote`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` explicitly blocks retrieval unless `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. That means an attacker cannot cause the server to fetch “arbitrary internal HTTP URLs” via `/embed/best?embed_url=...`; the URL host must match the configured `embeddable_host` or retrieval is skipped. The proposed finding overstates the impact (arbitrary internal SSRF) and is not directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer check is weak since referer is client-controlled

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is effectively authorized by comparing `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then setting `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`. The `Referer` header is client-controlled and can be spoofed in a direct HTTP request, so this check is not a strong/secure authorization mechanism. An attacker could supply a forged Referer matching the configured host and successfully load the embed endpoint (and trigger behavior like enqueuing `:retrieve_topic`) despite not actually being embedded by that host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of equality, allowing origins like https://eviltrout.com.attacker.net to bypass
Embed iframe posts resize message to request.referer which may be null/stripped, so resizing silently fails; should post to a consistent origin matching the receiver's check

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `request.referer` will typically be a full URL including a path/query (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/...`). The second argument to `postMessage` must be a valid *origin* (scheme + host + optional port) or `*`; passing a full URL is invalid and can throw a `SyntaxError`, preventing the resize message from being delivered (so resizing fails). This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff. While the controller enforces presence/host of `referer`, it does not ensure the value is reduced to an origin for `postMessage`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition in TopicEmbed.import: check-then-insert with no rescue of ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique causes concurrent imports to fail jobs and leave embed broken

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-insert: it first queries `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so concurrent imports of the same URL can both observe no row, both create posts, and then one `create!` will raise (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`). There is no rescue/retry around this, so the job/request can fail and can leave an extra created topic/post without a corresponding `topic_embeds` row, allowing repeated re-import attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If PostCreator succeeds but TopicEmbed.create! raises NotUnique, whole topic creation rolls back silently, wasting work repeatedly

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the “no embed” path does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then inside a `Topic.transaction` creates a post and then calls `TopicEmbed.create!`. Since the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, two concurrent imports of the same URL can both see `embed.blank?` and both create a topic/post; the second will hit the unique constraint and raise (e.g., ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique), which will roll back the whole transaction (wasting the post/topic creation work). The exception is not rescued here, so it will fail the caller/job rather than being “silent”, and it’s not necessarily “repeated” beyond retries, but the underlying race/rollback on NotUnique is a real, verifiable issue in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 update via update_column runs even if revisor.revise! returned false, causing sha drift

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1` differs it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. From the diff, `PostRevisor#revise!` explicitly `return false if not should_revise?`, so it can fail/skip the revision. In that case the post would not be updated but `content_sha1` would still be advanced, causing the stored sha to no longer correspond to the post’s content and potentially preventing future updates from being detected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor change makes validate: !skip_validations apply globally to all revisions when flag passed, silently removing validation for existing callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` (validations run) to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning callers passing `skip_validations: true` will now bypass validations. However, the finding claims this is a problematic silent behavior change for “existing callers,” which is not verifiable from the diff: we can’t see prior callers relying on `skip_validations` while still expecting validations to run, and the new code explicitly opts into skipping validations (and is immediately used that way by the new `TopicEmbed.import` path). This looks like intentional support for the `skip_validations` flag rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed crashes with NoMethodError on nil.scrub for Atom feeds using summary or items without content, aborting the entire polling run mid-loop
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root cause: the code calls `.scrub` on `i.content` assuming it exists, but some feeds/items lack a `content` field (e.g., Atom using summary/description), causing a NoMethodError on nil and crashing the polling loop. Candidate additionally mentions aborting mid-loop, which is consistent with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed i.link/i.id fallback can yield non-http url which import silently drops with no logging, causing partial silent import failures

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, the URL is taken from `i.link` and if it’s blank or not `http(s)` it falls back to `i.id` (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Many feeds use non-HTTP IDs (e.g., `urn:uuid:...`), so this fallback can still be non-HTTP. TopicEmbed.import immediately returns without creating/updating anything unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, and PollFeed does not log or otherwise surface that an item was dropped. This can cause silent, partial import failures for feed items with non-http link/id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) has no open_timeout/read_timeout or size limit, allowing hostile/slow URLs to block sidekiq workers indefinitely or download gigabytes into memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple `open-uri` calls without any explicit timeouts or response size limits: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). Both are executed from background jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed` scheduled job and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), so a slow/unresponsive URL can tie up Sidekiq threads, and an extremely large response can be read fully into memory (`.read`) or streamed into the RSS parser without bounds. This is a concrete risk directly present in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls misses protocol-relative //evil.com URLs and relative paths without leading slash

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links are only rewritten when `href`/`src` starts with `'/'` (see the `start_with?('/')` checks for both `a['href']` and `img['src']`). That means protocol-relative URLs like `//evil.com/x` and other relative forms like `foo/bar`, `../img.png`, or `./page` are not converted to absolute URLs, despite the method comment saying it converts “any relative URLs to absolute”. This can lead to embedded/imported HTML containing broken or unintended links/images.

adjudication_records.issue_text: URI(url) on attacker-supplied embed_url can raise uncaught URI::InvalidURIError inside import, killing the job

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. That allows many strings that still make `URI(url)` raise `URI::InvalidURIError` (e.g., bad percent-encoding like `http://example.com/%zz`). `TopicEmbed.import` calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, which does `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue. This can therefore raise uncaught and abort callers such as the scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` (which imports external feed item links) or `import_remote`/other import paths. So the diff introduces a real, verifiable unhandled-exception risk; the “attacker-supplied” part is plausible via external feed content even if the embed controller path filters some invalid URLs earlier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is non-standard and may be treated as DENY in some browsers, breaking embedding despite controller granting access

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`. `ALLOWALL` is not a standard/recognized X-Frame-Options directive (common valid values are `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and historically `ALLOW-FROM`). Using a non-standard value can cause browsers to ignore the header or handle it inconsistently, which can undermine the intended embedding behavior (either failing to allow framing as expected or behaving differently across browsers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus thor regression: --category option removed so posts lose their category

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the `--category` (`-c`) option and the associated lookup (`category_id = Category.where...`) were removed. Previously the importer passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`, allowing imported threads to be created in the chosen category. The new code calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or set any category, so imported topics can no longer be assigned to the specified category and will fall back to the default behavior (likely uncategorized).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote which re-fetches remote content at import time, failing on dead/redirected links or importing unrelated current page content

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path was changed from creating a topic directly from the Disqus thread metadata (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]", created_at: ..., ...)`) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` and runs `ruby-readability` on the fetched HTML, meaning the Disqus import now depends on live HTTP fetches at import time and will import whatever the URL currently serves. This can fail outright (dead link/network error) or import different/redirected/unrelated current content compared to what the Disqus export represented, and there is no rescue/handling shown in the diff.
